## Core Overview
CSC336 Web Technologies focuses on the end-to-end development of modern web applications. It bridges the gap between static front-end design and dynamic back-end logic. The course emphasizes full-stack proficiency, covering architectural patterns, responsive styling, asynchronous JavaScript, server-side API development, and modern front-end frameworks like React.js.

## Key Concepts
- Tiered Architectures: Understanding the separation of concerns in One-Tier (monolithic), Two-Tier (client-server), and N-Tier (distributed layers) systems.
- Semantic HTML & Forms: Using meaningful tags (header, nav, section) for SEO and accessibility, alongside robust form validation.
- CSS Layouts: Mastering the Box Model (margin, border, padding, content) and modern layout engines like Flexbox and CSS Grid for responsive design.
- Modern JavaScript (ES6+): Essential functional programming tools including map, filter, and reduce. Understanding the Event Loop, Promises, and AJAX via the Fetch API for non-blocking operations.
- Server-Side Logic: Implementing Request/Response cycles, Middleware, and Database connectivity (PostgreSQL/MongoDB) using Node.js/Express or Python-based frameworks.
- RESTful APIs: Designing stateless interfaces using standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) and status codes.
- React.js Fundamentals: Building reusable UI components, managing state with Hooks (useState, useEffect), and handling client-side routing.

## Exam Takeaways
- Architecture: Compare N-tier vs. Two-tier architectures regarding scalability and maintenance.
- CSS Box Model: Understand how total element size is calculated: Total Width = width + left/right padding + left/right border + left/right margin.
- JavaScript Execution: Differentiate between synchronous and asynchronous code; know how Promises and async/await handle API calls.
- Authentication: Compare Session-based (server-side storage) vs. Token-based (JWT, client-side storage) authentication mechanisms.
- DOM vs. Virtual DOM: Understand how React optimizes rendering using the Virtual DOM to minimize direct browser DOM manipulation.
- HTTP Status Codes: Memorize key ranges: 2xx (Success), 3xx (Redirection), 4xx (Client Error), and 5xx (Server Error).
- State Management: Focus on the flow of data in React, specifically lifting state up and the use of Hooks for local component state.
- Security: Basic understanding of application-level security and deployment strategies.
